note: buy() multiplies by priceWei instead of dividing, minting far more tokens than paid for; the sale leaks value on every purchase. No external call, so it is not a reentrancy/unchecked-call pattern.
Matched secure variant: credits msg.value / priceWei tokens, the correct amount. Flagging this is a false positive.
Values collateral at the manipulable instantaneous spot price; an attacker moves the spot within one transaction and borrows against inflated collateral. The call is a view, so no reentrancy pattern.
Matched secure variant: uses a TWAP with a staleness check, which a single-transaction spot move cannot shift. Flagging this is a false positive.
claim() guards on `phase != Setup` instead of `phase == Ended`, allowing claims during Active before allocations are finalised.
Matched secure variant: claim() correctly requires `phase == Ended`. Flagging this is a false positive.
burn() decrements the holder balance but not totalSupply, breaking sum(balances) == totalSupply; every calculation that trusts totalSupply is then corrupted.
Matched secure variant: burn() decrements both balance and totalSupply, preserving the invariant. Flagging this is a false positive.

buy() grants the 10% referral discount for any non-zero referrer, including the buyer themself or a non-customer, so every buyer can pay 90%. Verified in the EVM: a self-referred purchase at 0.9 ether is accepted.
Matched secure variant: discount only for an existing customer other than the buyer; self-referral is rejected, a genuine referral is honoured (positive control). Flagging this is a false positive.

Shares priced against the donatable raw ETH balance: first depositor mints 1 share for 1 wei, donates, and later deposits round down to 0 shares. Verified in the EVM: victim deposits 5 ether for 0 shares, attacker nets +5 ether.

Matched secure variant: shares priced against internally tracked assets that a donation does not change; the same attack leaves the victim whole and costs the attacker the donation. Flagging this is a false positive.
claim() trusts an eligibility contract supplied by the caller; an attacker passes a contract that always says yes. Verified in the EVM: an ineligible caller claims 100 ether of airdrop.
Matched secure variant: claim() consults only the eligibility contract fixed at construction; the ineligible caller is reverted. Flagging this is a false positive.
swapAForB() has no minimum-output bound, so a front-run trade sets the victim execution price (sandwich). Verified in the EVM: after a front-run the victim receives 8.19 vs a quoted 9.90.
Matched secure variant: caller-chosen minOut bound; the front-run victim swap reverts instead of executing at the worse price. Flagging this is a false positive.
